findings.title: Possible NPE when the all-clients resource is missing
findings.body:
When there is no client-specific resource, `hasPermission(ClientModel, String)` falls back to `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...)` and passes the result straight into `getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource)`. `getResourceTypeResource` returns null in two cases:
- `supportsAuthorizationSchema` is false, e.g. admin permissions were disabled on the realm but the admin-permissions client still exists.
- The "Clients" resource does not exist. This is the case for any realm whose admin-permissions client was initialized before this change, because `init()` returns early when the client already exists.

In both cases the store dereferences a null resource and throws an NPE. The call chain is `canView(client)` → `canConfigure` → `canManage(client)`, so any FGAP-only admin (without the manage/view-clients roles) gets a 500 on basic client endpoints. Add a null check that returns false, as the sibling `hasPermission(String)` already does.

findings.title: New Clients scopes/resource are never provisioned for existing admin-permissions clients
findings.body:
`init()` returns immediately if `realm.getAdminPermissionsClient()` is non-null. Scopes and the per-type 'all-resource' resources are only created on first initialization.

Realms that enabled FGAP v2 before this change keep their old setup: they have no `Clients` resource and no `configure`, `map-roles-client-scope` or `map-roles-composite` scopes. For those realms:
- Creating a Clients permission with those scopes fails in `getScope` with "Scope [...] does not exist".
- Creating a per-client resource fails in `getOrCreateResource` with "No scopes found."
- Evaluation hits the null `Clients` resource path.

There is no migration or reconciliation step that adds the missing schema elements.

findings.title: getClientsWithPermission returns the resource-type name instead of client IDs
findings.body:
Per-client resources are created by `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` via `resourceStore.create(...)` without setting a type. So `resourceStore.findByType(server, "Clients", ...)` only finds the 'all-clients' resource whose type was set in `init()`. The method then adds `resource.getName()`, which is the literal string "Clients", to the result set.

Callers expect a set of client IDs, as the V1 implementation returns. They will get either an empty set or `{"Clients"}`, never the clients the admin actually has the scope for. Any filtering based on this method is therefore wrong.

findings.title: Global canView() ignores all-clients MANAGE, inconsistent with canView(ClientScopeModel) and V1 semantics
findings.body:
`canView()` only checks the `view` scope on the all-clients resource. An admin granted MANAGE on all clients therefore gets `canView()` == false.

The inherited `canViewClientScopes()`, `canListClientScopes()` and `requireList()` all delegate to `canView()`. As a result, such an admin can manage every client scope (`canManageClientScopes`/`canManage(ClientScopeModel)` accept MANAGE) and `canView(ClientScopeModel)` explicitly accepts MANAGE. Yet the same admin gets 403 when listing client scopes or clients, unless they also hold a query-* role.

In V1, manage implies view (`canManageClientsDefault() || canViewClientDefault()`). Consider `hasPermission(VIEW) || hasPermission(MANAGE)` here. This also lets client listing use the paginated fast path instead of loading every client and evaluating it individually.

findings.title: Same resource evaluated repeatedly per client check
findings.body:
`canView(ClientModel)` calls `canView()`, then `canConfigure(client)`, which calls `canManage(client)`, then `hasPermission(client, VIEW)`. That is up to four full policy evaluations for one client:
- one of the all-clients resource;
- three of the same client resource, each evaluating all of its scopes and then discarding all but one.

The fallback path also runs a `findByResource` policy lookup each time. Client listing calls this for every client when global view is not granted, multiplying policy-evaluation cost. Evaluate the resource once and check for any of the accepted scopes.

findings.title: getResourceName not extended for the Clients resource type
findings.body:
`getResourceName` only special-cases `USERS`, returning "All users" or the username. For Clients-type permissions it falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()`.

Neither the 'Clients' all-resource nor the per-client resources (created with only a name) set a display name. Permission resource listings for client permissions will therefore show null instead of "All clients" or the clientId.

findings.title: Client deletion leaves orphaned V2 client resources/permissions
findings.body:
The removal listener is now a no-op unless V1 `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` is enabled. Nothing replaces it for V2.

With this PR, V2 creates per-client resources in the admin-permissions client, named after the client UUID. When a client is deleted, its resource and the scope permissions referencing it stay in the admin-permissions resource server indefinitely. The gate also silently removes the cleanup of leftover V1 data that previously ran regardless of the feature flag.

findings.title: Existing management/permissions endpoints now fail with 500 under V2
findings.body:
`isPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel)`, `setPermissionsEnabled` and `getPermissions` now throw `UnsupportedOperationException`. `ClientResource`'s `management/permissions` GET/PUT endpoints call these via `AdminPermissions.management(...).clients()`.

Before this PR, under V2 those endpoints returned a disabled reference. Now they surface as an unhandled 500 instead of a meaningful client error.

findings.title: Javadoc for void require* methods says "Returns true"
findings.body: The Javadoc on `requireView()` (line 96) and `requireViewClientScopes()` (line 101) says "Returns {@code true} if ... returns {@code true}". These methods are void and actually throw ForbiddenException when the corresponding `can*` method returns false.

findings.title: Test mutates the admin's own login client by removing an arbitrary default scope
No test that Users permissions don't leak to Clients via shared scopes
findings.body:
`init()` collapses scope names across resource types into a single Scope entity. 'manage', 'view' and 'map-roles' are now shared between the Users and Clients resource types, so isolation depends entirely on permissions being bound to the correct type resource.

No test checks either direction:
- that an all-users MANAGE/VIEW permission does not grant `canManage`/`canView` on clients;
- that a Clients permission does not grant user access.

`testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient` grants both types at once, so it cannot detect leakage. The `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE` scope and per-client negative overrides are also untested.
